# Where does FUSE beat Dawid-Skene? (generated by scripts/sim_regime_map.py)

AUC against the true label, mean over 6 seeds. Base setting: 1000 items, 10 raters, continuous scores, dense, 30% positive, rater separation d uniform on [0.5, 1.5] (single-rater AUC 0.64-0.86), no correlation. Each table changes one thing. 'best FUSE - best D&S' compares the better FUSE variant with the better Dawid-Skene variant in each run.

### Correlated raters

A cluster of raters shares part of its noise (rho = 0.6). 'weak' cluster: d = 0.3; 'junk' cluster: d = 0 (no signal at all).

| cluster | MV | D&S | D&S 5 bins | Mean z | FUSE logistic | FUSE product | best FUSE - best D&S (± s.e.) |

| 40% weak, correlated | 83.5 | 67.4 | 64.1 | 87.7 | 82.3 | 77.9 | **+15.0** ± 4.4 |

## Hypothesis: many non-experts on a hard question

Non-experts have separation d (all equal, spread none; d = 0.1 means single-rater AUC ~ 0.53); 2 of the raters are experts with d = 1.5, whatever the panel size. Rows: number of raters; columns: how hard the question is for the non-experts.

### Continuous scores



Cell = best FUSE AUC - best Dawid-Skene AUC (positive = FUSE wins); in brackets, best D&S AUC.
